title: Contactor Module — Installation in the Forward Primary Distribution Centre

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

ata.title: Electrical Load Distribution — Primary Distribution Centre

abstract: Installation of a contactor module and its auxiliary contact block in the forward primary distribution centre, with the interface bracket fitting rule and the post-installation functional test.

sections.purpose: This task gives the procedure to install a contactor module and its auxiliary contact block in the forward primary distribution centre, and the functional test that must follow before the aircraft is released.
sections.job_setup_note: The interface bracket is required at the two outboard positions on aircraft at the latching module standard and must not be fitted at the inboard position. Mounting screws are single use and must be renewed at every installation. The distribution centre must remain de-energised until the functional test step. A calibrated torque screwdriver is required; the screws are loaded in tension against a bonded insert and an over-torqued screw pulls the insert.
sections.procedure: 1. Make sure that the aircraft is on no external power and that the warning notices are in position. 2. Remove the protective cover from the rack position. 3. Clean the rack contact faces and apply a thin film of the electrical contact lubricant. 4. At an outboard position, install the interface bracket. CAUTION: DO NOT FIT THE INTERFACE BRACKET AT THE INBOARD POSITION. THE MODULE WILL SEAT BUT THE STATUS WIRING WILL NOT REACH. 5. Put the module in position, keeping it square to the rack, and push it home by hand until the rear connector is felt to engage. 6. Install four new mounting screws and tighten them equally, one turn at a time, to 3.5 Nm. 7. Install the auxiliary contact block. 8. Connect the status wiring and do a continuity check between the block and the rack terminal. 9. Install the module identification plate for the standard fitted. 10. Install the rack front cover. WARNING: MAKE SURE THAT NO TOOL OR LOOSE ARTICLE IS LEFT IN THE RACK BEFORE YOU CLOSE THE COVER. 11. Restore electrical power. 12. Do the distribution centre functional test and record the contact resistance at each position. 13. Command the module open and closed twice and confirm that the status wiring follows.
sections.close_out: Close the forward avionics bay access. Remove the warning notices. Record the module part number and the measured contact resistance in the aircraft maintenance record. Return the removed module in an antistatic bag with the removal reason attached.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Step 4 applies only to aircraft post MOD-146420.

safety_precautions: Put the warning notices in position in the flight compartment.
Make sure that the aircraft is on no external power until step 11.
